explanation:
# Place and route summary: spi_master (sky130A, sky130_fd_sc_hd, clk 50 MHz)

## Iteration table
| Iter | Parameters changed | What changed | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (it1) | none (first run, starting values) | Nothing; no changes were needed | route DRC 0, antenna 0, setup and hold positive in all 9 corners |

Starting parameters for it1: FP_CORE_UTIL 45, PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT 55.0, MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT 10, CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_SIZE 25, GRT_ANTENNA_ITERS 3, GRT_ANTENNA_MARGIN 10, CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_MAX_DIAMETER 50, CTS_DISTANCE_BETWEEN_BUFFERS 0, CTS_CLK_MAX_WIRE_LENGTH 0. The iteration log lists no problems and no changes, so the iteration budget (default 8) was not used beyond 1 run.

## Final state (iteration 1, from reports/pnr_iterations.json)
- Routing DRC errors: 0.
- Antenna: 0 violating nets, 0 violating pins.
- Disconnected pins: 0.
- Max slew violations: 0. Max cap violations: 0.
- Max fanout violations: 8 reported at limit 10. All 8 are clock-tree buffer outputs (clkbuf_3_0 to clkbuf_3_7 __f_clk/X) with fanout 11 to 17. The tool data marks them as allowed under the clock-tree net rule (limit 20). The independent DRV check lists no other violating pins (independent_drv_pins is empty).
- Wirelength: 13351 um. Utilization after routing: 0.559855 (floorplan utilization was 0.479564 on a 12061.6 um2 core, 16277.3 um2 die; power grid violations 0).
- Congestion / routing overflow: the input files contain no congestion or overflow figure, so I cannot quote one. See open issues.

## Timing (independent STA, 9 corners)
- Worst setup slack: 8.938063875351261 ns (max_ss_100C_1v60). Best corner: 9.799866973073428 ns (max_ff_n40C_1v95). All 9 corners are positive.
- Worst hold slack: 0.1040085824683123 ns (min_ff_n40C_1v95). All 9 corners are positive (largest 0.8687554255212969 ns at max_ss_100C_1v60).
- Setup slack by corner (ns): nom_tt 9.788, nom_ss 8.955, nom_ff 9.794, min_tt 9.782, min_ss 8.972, min_ff 9.789, max_tt 9.795, max_ss 8.938, max_ff 9.800.
- Hold slack by corner (ns): nom_tt 0.316, nom_ss 0.863, nom_ff 0.106, min_tt 0.313, min_ss 0.858, min_ff 0.104, max_tt 0.319, max_ss 0.869, max_ff 0.108.
- REQ-021 asks for setup and hold slack of at least 0 ns in every evaluated corner. The numbers above are positive in all 9 corners; the runtime checks make the final decision.

## Clock tree (reports/cts_report.json)
- 9 clock buffers; worst tree skew 0.007598 ns (max_ss_100C_1v60, hold side) against a 2.0 ns target from the tool data (the spec states no skew target).
- Tree skew is the reported skew minus the 0.25 ns clock uncertainty.
- 79 hold buffers and 178 timing-repair buffers were inserted (reported separately from the clock buffers).
- Post-CTS hold slack (3 nominal corners only): nom_tt 0.301475 ns, nom_ss 0.6181605402523026 ns, nom_ff 0.013112872270280695 ns. The nom_ff margin is thin (about 13 ps) at the CTS stage; the later final STA shows 0.10580808750866945 ns at nom_ff.
- Post-CTS setup slack (3 nominal corners): nom_tt 9.76201 ns, nom_ss 7.035543902160927 ns, nom_ff 9.576872010932588 ns.

## Notes
- No parameter was changed, so no pnr_ranges.yaml limit was touched and no waiver or rule change was made.
- I ran no tool in this task; every figure is quoted from the input files.
assumptions: The data in reports/pnr_iterations.json iteration 1 is the final state, since it is the only iteration.
The 8 max-fanout entries on clkbuf_3_*__f_clk/X are allowed because the tool data labels them 'clock-tree net, limit 20' and all values (11 to 17) are within 20.
Slack values are quoted from the independent STA data (setup_ws_by_corner, hold_ws_by_corner); post-CTS values come from cts_report.json.
Final decision on pass or fail belongs to the runtime checks, not to this summary.
open_issues: No congestion or routing overflow figure is present in the input files, so congestion state is not quoted.
Hold slack is the thinnest margin: 0.1040085824683123 ns at min_ff_n40C_1v95 in final STA, and 0.013112872270280695 ns at nom_ff_n40C_1v95 right after CTS.
Maximum fanout limit 10 is exceeded on 8 clock-tree buffer outputs (11 to 17); allowed by the clock-tree rule (limit 20) in the tool data, but a human may want to confirm that rule is acceptable.
PDK and library choice, and the IO delay and area values, are marked DEFAULT - needs G1 review in the spec.
